units.title: Holm clearance contract reaches its deadline
units.author: courier
units.text: The 30-day contract to clear Kittering Holm of trees ends today. Neither Grieve Land Services nor the island's owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, would tell the Courier whether the work has been completed, how many trees remain, or when the crew who have lived on the island for a month are expected to return to the mainland.

units.author: courier
units.text: The contractor's supply boat made its last booked crossing from Gilliver this morning and returned before ten. Gilliver's harbourmaster said he had received no booking for further sailings to the island. The boat's skipper told other harbour users he was 'on standby'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Grieve Land Services said in a short statement that it was 'completing the agreed programme' and that crew transport would be arranged 'in consultation with the client'. The firm did not say when that consultation would take place. Ardent Vale Holdings said it did not comment on operational matters.

units.author: courier
units.text: From Gilliver, residents continue to report lights at the island's camp every night, and fishermen working near the Holm say they have seen people on the shore in recent days. Estimates of how much of the island has been cleared vary widely and cannot be checked from the mainland.

units.author: courier
units.text: Several readers have written to the Courier this week asking that their good wishes be passed to the crew. In Gilliver, where many households keep a lamp in a seaward window by long custom, more lamps than usual were lit along the harbour front last night. 'It's only manners,' one resident said.

units.title: Live: last day of the Holm contract, what we know
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:30: Good morning. Today is the final day of the clearance contract on Kittering Holm. We'll bring you what we can confirm through the day, and we'll say clearly what we can't. The contractor's workboat left Gilliver at 06:35 for what the harbour office says is its last booked crossing.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:50: The workboat is back alongside at Gilliver. A listener on the harbour wall says it brought back equipment and waste skips. We have not been able to confirm whether any crew members were aboard; the harbourmaster says nobody disembarked who was not already on the boat.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:00: We asked Grieve Land Services when the crew will leave the island. A spokesperson said transport would be 'confirmed with the client in due course'. We asked Ardent Vale Holdings the same question and have not had a reply.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:30: A creel fisherman who works the water around the Holm tells us he saw people on the shore this morning near the camp, and that one of them waved. He did not want to be named and would not guess how much of the island had been cleared.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:00: Darkness has fallen over the Sound. The camp lights on the Holm are visible from Gilliver, as on every night this month. Along the harbour front, lamps are lit in a large number of windows. The weather is calm and clear, with frost expected.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 20:45: That's where things stand tonight: the contract period has ended, no crew transfer has been announced, and both companies say arrangements will follow. We'll pick this up in the morning bulletins. Thank you for your messages, and to those of you who asked: we are passing on every good wish we can.

units.title: Port Ammet harbour festival dates announced
units.author: courier
units.text: Next summer's Port Ammet harbour festival will run over three days in early July, organisers have confirmed, with a tall ship visit, a rowing regatta between the Sound's villages and a fish supper on the quay. Last year's festival drew an estimated twelve thousand visitors.

units.author: courier
units.text: The regatta will include a new race for crews from Lisle, Gilliver and Port Ammet in traditional four-oared boats. Gilliver last won the trophy in 1987 and its rowing club says it intends 'to put that right, finally'. Training starts in the spring.

units.author: courier
units.text: Organisers are looking for volunteers to marshal the quay and run the children's tent. Stall applications open in February. The festival committee thanked the lifeboat station for agreeing, once again, to lead the parade of boats.

units.title: Dellow Court lights 'working fine' as residents plan a party
units.author: weypost
units.text: Stairwell lighting at Dellow Court is 'working fine and will stay that way', the block's managing agent says, a month after residents first complained of lights failing between the sixth and eighth floors. A replacement timer relay was fitted earlier this month.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association said that while the lights were now reliable, some residents still preferred to use the lift at night, 'which is entirely their business'. A long-running dispute over a refuse chute seal causing smells in the lift is expected to be resolved next week.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents are now planning a Christmas party in the block's community room, with a sponsored stair climb by a tenant who is a personal trainer to raise money for decorations. The association secretary said she wanted 'the building to be known for something cheerful for a change'.

units.title: City publishes winter gritting routes
units.author: weypost
units.text: Weyhaven's highways department has published its winter gritting routes, with priority given to bus routes, hospital approaches and the port access road. Thirty-one gritters will be on standby from tonight, as the cold spell continues.

units.author: weypost
units.text: For the first time, pavements outside residential tower blocks will be included in the second-priority routes, after complaints of falls during the recent power cuts, when many residents walked home in darkness. The department said this would add about two hours to each overnight run.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Residents can check whether their street is on a route using the council's online map. The department reminds drivers that gritted roads can still be icy and asks them not to overtake gritters while they are spreading.

units.title: Grieve declines to comment on Holm completion
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services has declined to say whether it has completed the clearance of Kittering Holm, on the day its 30-day contract was due to end. A spokesperson said only that the firm was 'completing the agreed programme' and that it did not discuss client matters.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Industry observers say the outcome matters beyond the Holm. 'If they've done it, every client in the region will want thirty-day contracts,' said one contracts manager. 'If they haven't, nobody will touch a fixed deadline on an island again for years.' Both outcomes remain possible on the evidence available.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings has not responded to the Journal's questions about further works on the island. Earlier this week, the company described reports about its wider property holdings as 'misrepresented' while declining to say what those holdings are.

units.title: Tollinby traders welcome settled spell
units.author: courier
units.text: Market traders in Tollinby say the calm, dry weather of the past week has brought shoppers back to the town centre after a difficult month of storms, rain and power cuts. Saturday's market had its busiest day since the summer, according to the market manager.

units.author: courier
units.text: A hardware shop on Market Row reported selling out of small table lamps twice in a week. The owner said customers had mostly asked for something 'to leave on in the window', and that he had ordered more from Weyhaven. A candle stall on the market said its sales were up by half.

units.author: courier
units.text: The town's car park, a subject of complaint in this newspaper's letters page, will be resurfaced in the new year. The council says the work will be done in sections so that the market can continue throughout.

units.title: Sound Lines confirms winter timetable
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound Lines has confirmed its winter timetable for the Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver route, starting on the 3rd. The first morning sailing from Lisle moves five minutes later, to 07:15, and the Sunday night crossing is suspended until spring.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The weekday and Saturday 22:40 crossings continue with the new deck floodlights, which the operator says are now permanent. Commuters had feared further cuts to night sailings after the recent crew welfare review, which reduced the late service for almost a week.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: A regular Lisle commuter, who says he has kept a record of every crossing this month, told Sound FM the service had been 'better than its reputation and worse than its timetable'. Sound Lines said it would take that as a compliment.

units.title: Brackwater reservoir car park to close at dusk this winter
units.author: courier
units.text: The car park at Brackwater reservoir will be locked at dusk from next week until the end of February, the estate that manages the site has announced. The estate says the change follows several incidents of cars being left overnight and of people walking the reservoir paths after dark, which it described as 'unsafe in winter conditions'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The estate's ranger said that nobody had been hurt, but that staff had twice found the same car in the car park on consecutive mornings and had been 'more worried than we needed to be'. The owner turned out to be safe and well, he said, and had simply been staying elsewhere.

units.author: courier
units.text: Wildlife recordists and birdwatchers who use the reservoir at dawn will be able to request a key from the estate office. The ranger said daylight visitors were 'always welcome', and asked dog walkers to keep to the marked paths around the north inlet, where the bank is soft.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, 30th
units.author: met
units.text: Today: another dry, bright and cold day, light southeasterly winds. Maximum 6 degrees. Tonight: clear at first with a sharp frost, cloud thickening from the south towards dawn. Minimum minus 3 inland, 1 on the coast. Tomorrow: cloudier and less cold, with a little drizzle on southern coasts later.

units.title: Inshore waters, Carrow Point to Weyhaven
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters, next 24 hours. Wind southeast 3 or 4, occasionally 5 later in the south. Sea smooth or slight. Fair, becoming cloudy later. Visibility good, occasionally moderate later. No warnings in force.

units.title: Tide times, Gilliver, 30th
units.author: met
units.text: Gilliver tides: low water 00:10 (0.7 m) and 12:25 (0.6 m); high water 06:12 (4.4 m) and 18:31 (4.5 m). Approaching springs. Half-tide windows for small landings around 09:20 and 15:30. The Holm landing approach dries around low water.

units.title: Outlook: the days ahead
units.author: met
units.text: Outlook. The high that has given a week of settled weather will drift away eastwards over the next two days. Expect more cloud, milder nights and occasional drizzle, mainly in the south. Winds stay mostly light. No severe weather is expected in the coming days.

units.title: Service update, 30th
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines: all sailings are operating to the timetable today, including the 22:40 night crossing. The current timetable remains in force until the 2nd; the winter timetable begins on the 3rd. Passengers are asked to take care on frosted ramps.

units.title: Night crossings this winter
units.author: ferry
units.text: Customer notice: night crossings will operate on weekdays and Saturdays throughout the winter timetable. Boarding after dark is by the floodlit ramp only, under crew supervision. Foot passengers waiting at Gilliver after dark are asked to wait inside the shelter until called.

units.author: power
units.text: Planned work in Tollinby north is complete and supplies were restored at 12:41, ahead of schedule. Thank you for your patience. If your supply has not returned, please check your trip switches before contacting us.

units.title: Network update: insulator programme
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op network update: the insulator replacement programme on coastal spans will continue in daylight hours through the next month. The network remains in its normal running arrangement. To report a fault at any hour, use the number on your bill or our website.

units.title: Bins: weekend and next week
units.author: council
units.text: Collections next week will run on normal days across the district. Garden waste collections finish for the winter at the end of next week. Residents with garden waste subscriptions will be contacted about renewal in February.

units.title: Library opening hours: consultation reminder
units.author: council
units.text: Reminder: the consultation on library opening hours in Port Ammet, Tollinby and Lisle closes on the 12th. Proposals include later opening on two weekday evenings during the winter months. Paper forms are available at every branch.

units.author: coast
units.text: Update to notice to mariners: the contractor's workboat completed its notified crossing to the Kittering Holm landing stage this morning and has returned to Gilliver. No further movements to the Holm have been notified. The private temporary light at the landing stage continues to be exhibited.

units.author: coast
units.text: The Gilliver inshore lifeboat training exercise in the harbour approaches has been completed. Thank you to harbour users for keeping clear. The station's next public exercise will take place in the new year.

units.author: coast
units.text: Cancellation: the advice on sea smoke near coasts is withdrawn as milder, cloudier air arrives from the south. Normal precautions apply. Mariners are reminded that visibility in drizzle can fall quickly on southern approaches.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec 18th. Calm & clear again. Tally 14. The far lines given up entirely by the foreman's word; we work the shore side only now, where the lamps can be seen from the huts. Wages to the 16th. Nine on the roll. McCrory asks me to write that he is well, for his mother, & so I have.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec 19th. Calm. Tally 11. The foreman says we shall have the boat Thursday and I am to make up the wages book to the day. The men are quiet. I have trimmed the lamps and will sit up with

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: [Transcriber's note: the entry ends here, at the foot of a page. The remaining leaves are blank. A loose slip inside the back board, in a different hand, reads 'Nine paid off at Gilliver, 22nd'. Whether the slip belongs to this camp, or to this volume, is not known.]

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan 31. 00:00 wind S 4, overcast, visibility moderate. 02:00 lamp checked. 04:00 lamp checked, burning well. Remarks: Assistant keeper Dunmore left by the noon boat, his relief arriving on the same. Relief appears a steady man. I have shown him the log and the lamp and the road. Remarks column otherwise blank this watch.

units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day eight, and last. Boatman came at noon, not four, and would not wait while I finished the north transect; he said the weather was turning, though I saw no sign of it. Packed in a hurry. Summary for the survey: birds, ample; hares, ample; deer, none found, though browse suggests otherwise. I make no further remark. [The notebook continues on the next page with the survey of Lisle.]

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Mar 2. Wind west at last, soft. Tam went out the Holm side this morning as if nothing and came back with a good catch and a grin. I asked him what changed. He said the weather. Mother has put the lamp back on the dresser. Lobster 9d. Paid off the coal man in full.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Editor's addition: on the last evening of the month, lamps were reported in most seaward windows on Gilliver's harbour front and in a number of houses in Tollinby and Weyhaven, where the custom has no recorded history. The society notes this without interpretation. [citation needed: press and personal reports only; a proper survey would be welcome.]

units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Final talk note for this page, as I am going away for the winter. I accept that the wages were paid. I accept that the men kept lamps lit all night and gave up the far lines. I do not accept that any of this requires an explanation beyond cold, dark and a foreman with sense. If someone finds a document saying otherwise, I will read it with interest. Until then the page should say 'reasons unknown', and nothing more. Pell

units.title: Oral history project, Gilliver, 1974: tape 17 (one speaker, unfinished)
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: INTERVIEWER: Some people say the lamp is for the dead. SPEAKER: Some people say a lot of things. My aunt said that. My aunt also said the Holm was full of wolves, and there's never been a wolf in the Sound. [pause] No, it's not for the dead. INTERVIEWER: Then who? SPEAKER: It's for whoever's still out. That's all. [Tape ends; side B blank.]

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LBA-2225. Date: 1960s, summer (donor's estimate). Location: Gilliver harbour, near the inn. Kit: reel-to-reel portable, mono, slow speed. Duration 22 min. Description: fiddle (slightly flat), conversation indistinct, dog, gulls, ferry horn at 06:10 and 18:55. Percussive events: none. Curator's note: digitised and donated by hobby_tapeloop. A pleasant file.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: Your correspondent has been taken to task by three readers over the date of the timber men's return, which one gives as before Christmas, one as Twelfth Night and one as 'the hard frost, whenever that was'. He records all three and favours none. All agree the men came home by boat, and that the village lamps were lit for them, as is only proper.

units.title: Relay station survey: covering letter (1950s)
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Sir, I enclose the completed survey of Kittering Holm. You will see that the site is suitable in all technical respects and that the cost is within the estimate. I must nevertheless repeat the recommendation in paragraph 14. I would add, privately, that I could not in conscience post a man there. I have nothing more specific to offer and would ask that this letter not be placed on the file. Yours faithfully.

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note, further. A reader in Lisle has offered three original issues from the winter in question, found in a sea chest. We will digitise them in the new year. She warns that two have been used to line a drawer and one has a recipe for mutton pudding written across the front page. We are grateful for all of it.

units.title: Final statement GLS-PR-3008: KH-01 contract close
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Final statement ref: GLS-PR-3008. Site: KH-01 Kittering Holm. Period: contract days 29 and 30, and contract close. The site account will be reconciled once final timesheets and the closing count are received. Release of the final contract balance is subject to reconciliation. Automated message; this mailbox is not monitored.

units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: AUTOMATED REMINDER, second notice. Account KH-01 still shows crew wages outstanding at contract close. The final contract balance is held until the account is clear. Reference ARR-KH01-30. Queries to your operations manager. Replies to this address are not read.

units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Scheduled reminder: timesheet submission for site KH-01 closes at 23:59 tonight. Timesheets received after this time will be processed in the next payroll cycle. If submission is not possible from site, your operations manager can accept photographs. Automated message.

units.title: Did you know? Belongings in transit
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Lyle Insurance tip of the month: your policy covers personal belongings in transit, including by sea, up to the limit shown in your schedule. Travelling home after a long job? Keep receipts for valuable tools and equipment. Peace of mind for every journey, however long it takes. Small print: business equipment is excluded unless declared.

units.title: New! Meet the Hearthglow Beacon
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: New in! Meet the Hearthglow Beacon, our brightest lantern ever: 72 hours on one charge, a warm-white glow and a hook for hanging in any window. Perfect for long nights, remote sites and anyone who likes to leave a light on! Thank you for being a Camp Supply customer this season. Enjoy 10% off your next order, all winter long!

units.title: With thanks
units.author: ardentvale_pr
units.text: As the current phase of work on Kittering Holm draws to a close, Ardent Vale Holdings would like to thank everyone who has contributed to it. Our commitment to patient, responsible stewardship of the island remains unchanged, and we look forward to sharing our long-term vision when the time is right. We have no plans to announce at this time. The Ardent Vale community information team

units.title: Today
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, first thing, as promised: - I still don't have transfer times from the client. I've chased twice since yesterday. - Our boat is on standby from tomorrow and the skipper will go as soon as I have word. - Please keep the crew and the essential kit together, and run the camp as normal until then. - Final count to me by 18:00, please. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the skipper says this morning's run went smoothly and everything on the list came back to the depot. Thank you. If there's anything you need before pick-up, put it on the next boat's list, whenever that is. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Final count
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, from what I can see the count is in a good place. Head office are drafting the note to the client. Please don't let anyone take risks on the last stems for the sake of a number; nobody upstairs will thank you for an injury on the final day. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Final count
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, as I said yesterday, if we're short at close, head office will review options with the client. I've been asked not to speculate about what those options are, and I'm not going to. What I can say is that you and the crew have worked hard all month, and I have said so upstairs, in writing. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Tonight
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office will be speaking to the client this evening about the position on the Holm. I'll pass on anything that affects you or the crew as soon as I'm told it. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the wages flag is still showing on the account. I can't hold the final payment request back any later than tonight, and when it goes in, the flag goes with it. Please. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the leaver's account is closed. I rang their family myself to confirm the final pay. They asked me to tell the rest of the crew they're thinking of them, so I'm telling you. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a short one. I've asked the client again for transfer times and been told 'shortly'. I'll write tomorrow as soon as I have anything at all. Thank you for this month, all of you, whatever the count says. Ruth

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello. My piece ran today. I wrote that the contract has ended and that nobody will say when the crew are coming home, because that is all I can stand behind. A number of readers have written in asking me to pass on their good wishes, which I am now doing. I'll keep asking Grieve about the transfer until I get an answer. Best wishes, Nell

units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: One more thing, since I promised I would pass on anything I was asked to. A man on the harbour wall at Gilliver this evening asked me to tell 'the lot on the island' that the front is lit for them tonight. I said I would try. I don't know if this reaches you. I hope it does. Nell

units.title: Last one, I promise
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Why did the feller lose his job? He couldn't make the cut. That's the last one, I've run dry. Proud of you, whatever the count. Drinks are on me when you're back. If the boat's late, it's late: keep everyone together, keep the fire in, and don't let anyone wander off. You know all that. Ignore me. Hal

units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: PS. I mean it about the drinks. The good pub, not the one by the depot. And you're buying the second round, because I bought the last one in about 2009 and I've been waiting. Hal

units.title: last day
units.author: sam
units.text: hi you. last day, the paper says. she's made a sign that says welcome home in glitter with the dog's paw print on the corner (the dog was not consulted). Mum's practising the walk to the car. Ruth hasn't rung about which harbour yet, so we'll wait. whatever happens, we're here. I've put a lamp in the front window. I don't know why, the woman on the radio said Gilliver people do it, and it felt right. love you. S x

units.author: sam
units.text: can't sleep again. it's gone midnight, so technically the contract's over. I hope you're asleep. if you're not, the lamp's still on here, and the dog's lying across the front door like he's waiting for someone. x

units.title: Last day
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello. The last day, they say. I'm fine. Tomas, if you're reading this over the boss's shoulder: I'm fine, I'm not cross, and the boiler is still working. Is he sleeping? Please tell him to sleep, whatever is happening. Ana

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello again. I still don't know if it was Tomas who left. If he's with you, tell him I'll be waiting wherever the boat comes in. If it was him, then I hope he's on his way to my sofa with his washing. Either way, I'm fine. Sorry. Ana

units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Sorry, one more. I put a lamp in my window tonight. My neighbour says it's a Gilliver thing. I'm in Weyhaven and I don't really know why I did it. It's nice, though. It makes the room feel like someone is expected. Ana

units.title: Gilliver tonight
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Hello. This is the last night of your contract, if the paper is right. Gilliver is lit tonight, more windows than I've ever seen. I counted from my window and stopped at sixty. I'm not saying it's for you. I think some of it is. I might be wrong. Please look after each other. M.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Sorry. Your jetty light is still on, and so is the one by the camp. I'm going to bed now. I hope you are too, or at least somewhere warm. M.
